synopsis: ISO 3450:2011, edition 4, confirmed in 2022, specifies minimum service, secondary and parking-brake performance and tests for wheeled earth-moving and rubber-tracked machines with top speeds of at least 20 km/h; purpose-built underground mining machines are outside its scope, although an annex provides modifications [f15190, f2433]. It measures stopping distance from brake-control actuation to standstill, including brake-system response but excluding operator reaction, and tests the most adverse braking configuration, including maximum specified payload for dumpers and certain other machines; controllability also matters, so stopping distance alone is insufficient [f5976, f5967, f5968, f6149]. The proposed four-month validation plan uses ISO 21815-3 CxS calculations for each machine model, supplied with ISO 3450 brake data and declared system delays, but passing ISO 3450 does not validate perception or collision-trigger logic [f2638, f2361]. ISO 3450 brake testing is physical, and the research found no provision allowing simulation to replace prescribed physical performance tests [f10431, f2475]. Its machine-performance tests do not establish statistical model transfer, and no defensible calibration-stop count was found for prediction across 100-plus site types, multiple brake architectures and all stated weather conditions [f6163, f6162]. Edition and source verification remain planning gaps: some chapters did not verify ISO 3450 details or its current edition, vendor-reported stopping formulas require checking against the standard, and the glossary says most core standards, including ISO 3450 in the listed group, are being reissued in late 2026 shortly before design freeze [f7013, f7741, f11197, f2436, f15013].
